response.overview: Over the last two decades, the Arctic permafrost has lost one meter of ground each year. As it melts, it uncovers carcasses from the Pleistocene Epoch. Buried in ice for millennia, these frozen bodies appear remarkably well preserved from time and material decay, sometimes maintaining fur, skin, and internal organs intact. Jarkov is a complete woolly mammoth who died 20,000 years ago. Upon discovery, instead of being excavated, he was removed as a single, solid mass along with the surrounding soil. As a result, the mammoth remains are encased in a block of permafrost, only displaying visible patches of skin and hair on the surface, as well as two tusks protruding from it.
response.title: Jarkov
